Amazon currently has it for $749.99 (originally $1,499.99), a 50% discount, and the lowest price it has ever been.

Samsung’s HW-Q600F soundbar is down to $379.97 at Amazon from $499.99, a $110 discount that brings it to its lowest price ever. This 2025 model sits in the middle of Samsung’s Q-Series lineup and pairs a sleek, angular bar with a subwoofer in a 3.1.2 setup. Dolby Atmos also brings a modest sense of height, and effects track cleanly from left to right. You get a graphic equalizer and sound presets for adjusting the audio to your preferences through the included remote.

The Ultimate Ears Miniroll is down to $49.99 (originally $79.99), the second-lowest it has sold for so far. It’s a small, flat, puck-shaped Bluetooth speaker that weighs just over half a pound, with a removable rubber strap you can attach to a backpack, bike handlebar, or shower caddy. Despite its size, the Miniroll can get surprisingly loud—which PCMag confirms in its review—and at moderate volume, it has enough sound for a kitchen or backyard without sounding thin. As for its battery life, you get about 12 hours of playback before it needs a charge over USB-C, while its IP67 rating protects it from dust and a brief dunk in water.

If you're looking for a premium model, Samsung’s 65-inch S90H OLED TV is down to $1,397.99 from $2,697.99 at launch, saving you over $1,000. The sale price is easier to justify when you consider that this is a new 2026 model. If the 65-inch model does not suit your space, Samsung also sells the S90H in 42-, 48-, 55-, 77-, and 83-inch versions, and those sizes are discounted as well.

It's already been a big week for movie news. Just a few days ago Robert Pattinson was announced as the new James Bond in the developing Denis Villeneuve movie. Fans of the James Bond movies were shook by this news, and the internet has been ablaze for days. Of course, Florence Pugh was the first person to text the filmmaker the casting arrived online.

In addition to fan responses to this 007 news, a number of celebrities have also weighed in. Brad Pitt had a big reaction, and it turns out that Pugh went straight to the source. At the Elle Women in Hollywood event (via Twitter) the Oscar-nominated actress shared her message to the Villeneuve, saying:

Honestly, the idea of Florence Pugh joining the next James Bond movie doesn't seem out of the question. The threequel also features Robert Pattinson as Scytale, and it seems like the Twilight alum impressed the director enough that he's brought him on to play everyone's favorite martini-sipping MI6 agent.

Pattinson's casting has been arguably the biggest entertainment story this week, with fans and fixtures of the business weighing in. This year alone he appeared in The Drama, The Odyssey, and Primetime, and he's currently filming Matt Reeves' The Batman: Part Two.

On the other hand, there are plenty of memes about just how many major franchises Robert Pattinson has managed to have a role in. After all he's appeared in Harry Potter, Twilight, Batman, Dune, and now James Bond. They say all publicity is good publicity, and it should be fascinating to see how this discourse influenced the upcoming 007 movie's box office performance.

Additionally, folks can see Pugh, Pattinson and Villeneuve's collaboration when Dune: Part Three hits theaters December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list.

Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie includes a lot of swearing, with main character Bryan (Austin Abrams) saying the words "f**k" and "shit" over and over again as he faces a nightmare in Raccoon City. But the film could have had a lot more swearing.

Cregger said in a new interview with Sony for the movie's home release, that, "The whole thing was carpeted with f**ks. You think there's a lot of f**ks in there now? You should have heard the rough cut. It was insane."

Abrams said he isn't sure how many of the swear words were written into the script, saying there was "definitely a lot improvised."

Cregger, who co-wrote the script with Shay Hatten, said the original script indeed had a lot more f**ks in it. "We tried to go in and take as many as we possibly could out of the movie. I think we probably pulled 70%," he said.

Cregger went on to joke that there is a "F**k Cut" of Resident Evil out there.

Similarly, there is a more comedic cut of the movie that exists. Test screenings showed that it was too funny. "So over the course of my testing, I stripped out as much of the jokes as possible,” he said previously.

Cregger was previously in the sketch comedy group Whitest Kids 'U Know and has some fantastic comedy chops. Perhaps one day we'll get to see Cregger's original version of Resident Evil with more swearing and more comedy.

The Resident Evil movie made more than $400 million globally and ranks as the highest-grossing film of Cregger's career and the top-grossing Resident Evil movie ever. Cregger won't come back for a sequel, though. He got a lot of hate from core gamers about his Resident Evil movie, which didn't feature any storylines or characters from the games, and is now pursuing only original movies as a director.

#3545. Three Ways to Avoid CAPTCHA Prompts When Using a VPN

VPNs make it harder to track your online activity across websites, but it also makes them suspicious about your origins. When you borrow an IP address that hundreds of other people are also using for any number of reasons, you’re much more likely to get repeat verification requests from online firewalls.

CAPTCHAs are simple puzzles that websites use to filter out bots and spam. They’re supposed to be easy for people but hard for robots, such as simple object recognition tasks or audio-visual challenges. However, they can still disrupt your browsing experience if they happen too frequently.

Most modern CAPTCHA providers, like Google's reCAPTCHA v3 or Cloudflare Turnstile, start working long before they give you a puzzle to solve. It usually starts with a risk score that studies your IP address, browser and device signals, or recent online activity.

If the CAPTCHA provider can’t confidently identify your request as human based on those signals, it requests that you complete a puzzle before deciding if the request should be blocked. That means when you get repeat CAPTCHA requests, there’s something affecting your browser’s risk score. For example, popular VPN servers spread the same IP address across any number of users, which can easily make a website mistake you for a bot farm. If you change your IP address frequently by switching servers often, that might look suspicious too.

Luckily, there are ways to deal with frequent CAPTCHA requests using tools and services available with your browser and VPN. Cloudflare has already cut its CAPTCHA requests by 91% using its Managed Challenge platform. Apple has also been shipping token-based verification on devices since iOS 16 and macOS Ventura. In June 2026, Cloudflare even announced a joint effort called the Private Access Control Tokens (PACT) standard with Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Shopify.

While there’s no direct off switch for CAPTCHAs, you can use different fixes to improve your browser’s trust signals when using the internet. That way, you’re less likely to be hounded by verification requests.

The easiest fix for repeat CAPTCHAs is to stop connecting to whichever server your VPN app picks automatically. Proton recommends choosing servers with lower traffic load. In fact, its apps display load as a percentage to help you avoid the most crowded options. I'd also skip big traffic hubs like New York or London, since that's where most traffic originates from. Servers in smaller cities located nearby are often just as fast but never as populated.

You should also avoid changing IP addresses too frequently, which can look suspicious on its own. Pick a server that seems to behave well, then continue using it for at least one session. Also remember you’re more likely to get premium server options if you’re on a paid VPN plan. Major platforms like ExpressVPN, Surfshark, Proton, and Nord are particularly likely to have a larger server collection to pick from.

Costs nothing more than your current subscription

Hopping between servers often can backfire

Private Access Tokens (PAT) let you verify the authenticity of your request using your device rather than an IP address. Apple calls it Automatic Verification, where an Apple server validates your device and Apple Account to assign you an anonymous token.

To enable Automatic Verification on an iPhone or iPad, go to Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification. On a Mac, open System Settings > [your name] > Sign-In & Security > Automatic Verification.

Unfortunately, there’s no equivalent feature for Windows, Android, and Linux users. That said, Cloudflare offers the Silk extension for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that serves a similar function. A quick look at the ratings will tell you it’s not as effective, but Cloudflare’s upcoming cross-browser standard called PACT seems promising once it is released.

Doesn’t share personal details with websites

Chrome and Firefox extensions can be unreliable

If you pay a bit extra for a dedicated IP add-on, VPN providers can assign you a unique IP address that isn’t shared with anyone else. For example, NordVPN offers dedicated IPs in 30 countries for $2-5 a month and Surfshark charges $3.75 a month for it.

There are also dedicated providers like Private Internet Access, which charges $3.99 per month for a zero-trust setup so not even their employees know which IP address is assigned to you. On the other hand, Proton VPN offers dedicated IPs only to business plan users, so you’ll need to be on the Workspace Standard, Premium, or Enterprise plans to get one.

That said, there is a trade-off here too. NordVPN itself admits that a dedicated IP makes it easier to link online activity back to a single user. Also, many websites can still tell that the IP address originated from a VPN data center rather than a consumer’s device.

Get unique IP addresses with pristine reputation

Works across desktop, mobile, and even smart TVs

Also functions as an allowlisted address for work

Add-ons cost more on top of the VPN subscription

Offers less anonymity than shared VPN servers

#3544. The GTA 6 Police Don’t Have Equal Response Times For All Crimes

As with all Grand Theft Auto games, in GTA 6, the police will come after you if you commit a crime with witnesses. However, their response time will not always be the same, and you may be able to use this to your advantage, depending on the situation.

As we learned during our time with Grand Theft Auto 6 so far, the police will respond more slowly if you are assaulting a gang hideout. Presumably, this is because the police force believes you're doing them a favor, but regardless, they will still show up if you get into an all-out firefight and make a bunch of noise.

We also found that, for this reason, using silenced weapons is extremely helpful, as the police will only be called if you are spotted or heard committing a crime. Of course, this is GTA, so you're still naturally going to screw up at some point and have a massive wave of police cars after you, but it doesn't need to happen all the time.

For more on GTA 6, including what to do first, you can check out our guides hub. You can also read our full Grand Theft Auto 6 review, which became the latest in a very small list of games to ever receive a 10/10 score.

#3543. Jennifer Lopez's Most Candid Quotes About Divorce From Ben Affleck

Jennifer Lopez has spent the past two years publicly processing her second split from Ben Affleck — and she has not held back about what the experience taught her.

The singer and actress filed for divorce from Affleck in August 2024 after two years of marriage, and the split was finalized in 2025. In the months since, Lopez has opened up across multiple interviews and podcasts about heartbreak, self-reflection and her new “happy era.”

From calling the breakup “disappointing” to describing it as “the best thing that ever happened,” here is a look at everything Lopez has said about her divorce.

Lopez delivered some of her most pointed remarks yet during an appearance on the “Friends Keep Secrets” podcast hosted by Benny Blanco in November 2026.

“It was such a hard, disappointing last situation on every level,” she told Blanco. “On every level, it was so disappointing. I don’t ever want to delve into that.”

The “On the Floor” singer admitted she has historically been “a serial monogamist, one after another, trying to find the thing, hoping that this was it.” Following her divorce from Affleck, she said she sat in her heartbreak and did the internal work. “It changed me. I allowed it to change me.”

Reflecting on her advice for anyone navigating a split — Lopez was previously married to Ojani Noa, Cris Judd and Marc Anthony — she said divorces are “hard” and “disappointing,” but she tries to hold herself to a standard.

“My advice for divorce is my advice for everything, which is, always operate in a way that you’ll feel proud of when you look back,” Lopez said. “I can look back at these situations and be like, even as painful as some of them were — so bad, life-shifting pain and hurt — I can look back and be like, I loved completely. I acted in a way that I’m proud of as a human.”

She added, “That’s my advice for anything, because when you go through hard things like that, it’s easy to kind of be like, ‘F*** this.’ You’re in so much pain, you want to hurt somebody else, or somebody has hurt you so much that you’re like … but you can’t.”

On a June 2026 episode of the “Smartless” podcast, Lopez got candid about hitting a breaking point after the split.

“There comes a point where it’s all so puzzling and wrong. Where you have to sit there. After my last divorce, I just sat there,” Lopez said. “I canceled my tour and I sat there, and I was like, ‘You need f***ing figure yourself out.’”

Lopez told the hosts she had to resist the urge to blame Affleck for the marriage’s collapse. “[I asked], ‘What is going on with you?’ Forget about everybody else. There’s nobody to blame here except yourself in a certain way,” she said. “Not that people don’t behave in a way that’s not great. But, ‘What are you doing? What do you have going on?’ That was a turning point for me.”

The singer said recognizing “patterns” allowed her to revisit her younger self. “Looking at those patterns, I was able to go back to that little girl [I once was] and really look at her. That little girl with the ripped nightgown — I can see her right now. … Dirty feet, walking around barefoot all the f***ing time. And just kind of going like, ‘You did this. You did all of this. Give yourself a little fing something. A little love! Stop looking for love in other things and give it to yourself.’”

Lopez credited her sister Lynda Lopez with urging her to be her own “keeper.” She added, “These are all little pieces. I feel like the journey is little puzzle pieces that you fit in little by little as you sit there with the oat milk and go, ‘It’s me.’”

Lopez expanded on her year of self-reflection during an appearance on Good Morning America in March 2026.

“I took a year off,” she explained, adding that she had to “stop everything” following the split. “I canceled tours. I decided to just be home and sit in what had happened without running away from it through work, through another person through anything. Just sit.”

The Atlas star said she needed to be present for her twins, Max and Emme, whom she shares with Anthony. “I was just at a point where I was like, ‘What is going on with you?’ I couldn’t blame anybody else because I don’t think that’s where the lesson is. And so, I really needed to figure myself out.”

More than a year later, Lopez described herself as being in her “happy era.”

“I feel like for the first time in my life, I’m free. I’m on my own. It feels really good. I didn’t really know what that felt like since I was in my early 20s, and even before that I always had a boyfriend,” she said. “I’ve gotten to the point where I really trust myself and appreciate myself a little bit more.”

As for dating again? “God forbid,” Lopez quipped. “I don’t want to ruin anything. It’s so nice right now. I’m so happy. It’s the best.”

In a September 2025 interview with CBS Sunday Morning, Lopez credited Affleck’s production company, Artists Equity, with helping bring her film Kiss of the Spider Woman to the screen — and then opened up about the contrast between her set life and home life.

“It was hard not to think about stuff, but it was, like, the best and the worst of times. Every moment on set … I was so happy. And then … back home, it was not great,” Lopez shared. “But you get through it and, you know, honestly, I have to say, it was the best thing that ever happened to me because it changed me. It helped me grow in a way that I needed to grow … become more self-aware. I’m a different person now than I was last year.”

Lopez called the summer following the divorce “probably the best summer I’ve ever had,” adding, “I realized that joy is in living … and really embracing life and everything that it brings to you. The hard times are the lessons and you have to understand that.”

Lopez first broke her silence on the divorce in an October 2024 cover story for Interview magazine with comedian Nikki Glaser.

“I think my whole life I’ve just been trying to say I’m good enough, until where I am now, when I know. I’m giving myself credit. I’m telling that little girl that grew up in the Bronx, ‘You’ve done really good for yourself,’” Lopez told Glaser. She acknowledged that after her recent projects, “my whole f***ing world exploded.”

Rather than searching for another partner, Lopez said she felt energized by independence. “Yes, I’m not looking for anybody, because everything that I’ve done over the past 25, 30 years, being in these different challenging situations, what can I f***ing do when it’s just me flying on my own — What if I’m just free?”

Warning! The following contains spoilers for the result of Dancing With The Stars Season 35 Semifinals. Stream the episode with a Disney+ subscription and read at your own risk!

In what's been one of the wildest two weeks I've seen in Dancing With The Stars, two frontrunners were eliminated before the finale. First, it was Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy, and now Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson will miss out on the finale when it hits the 2026 TV schedule. There's a lot of conversation about why this happened, but unlike some, I don't think it has anything to do with the pros, but rather their contestants.

Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Dewan are the latest to learn that Dancing With The Stars is more than a skills competition. Popularity with the fans is a real thing, and as the fandom rallies behind Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik, the obvious takeaway is that their previous dance experience hurt them more than it helped when it came to the votes.

Dancing With The Stars' casting team has gotten more brazen over the past few seasons when it comes to bringing in contestants who have professional dancing experience. Harry and Jenna aren't the first cases of this, but after watching the first few weeks of Season 35, it was clear they were leagues above the rest of the field.

For me, and I'm assuming many others, the fun of Dancing With The Stars is watching the competitors improve over the course of the competition. It's why I wrote about there being a consolation prize for the most improved dancer.

Fortunately we didn't need it, because the fans decided they wanted Tatyana, this season's clear choice for most improved, in the finale. It's my hope that, as the pros and contestants speak their piece about this season, the producers see the real message behind it all. We want more competitors who are a blank slate with room for improvement, and fewer polished dancers in the mix.

For those upset that Jenna and Harry missed the chance to compete in the finale, rest assured they will likely still be involved in Dancing With The Stars' 2026 ender. Eliminated contestants are often brought back for group performances and other fun while the other contestants prep for their dances.

DWTS' Glee Tribute Made Me Cry, But What Was Going On In The Background Made Me Irate

And just to say it, Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Dewan didn't need the mirrorball trophy to prove they were accomplished dancers. Being featured in music videos with major pop stars already did that for them, but I can understand the disappointment in falling short after weeks of competing.

I would argue this win means a lot more to the remaining competitors, especially with the fandom bucking the trend of voting for the best dancer. Someone is going to win after knowing next to nothing about ballroom dancing, and that's worth the excitement.

For the fans, I'd also argue this is the most exciting outcome. For me the finale just went from a predictable night in which everyone celebrates Harry's win, to a wide open field in which any one of them could win it all. It makes it all that much more exciting, and I can hardly wait until next week.

#3539. Rockstar Founder Issues Rare Statement As GTA 6 Launches To Superb Reviews And Huge Sales

We might not hear from him much, but Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser remains highly involved with the studio and its games, and that includes GTA 6, which is available now in New Zealand and everywhere else on November 19.

To mark the game's launch, Houser released a statement in which he said Rockstar has once again tried to create a game in GTA 6 that "exceeds your expectations" and shows "what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special."

He told GamesRadar: "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with us."

The executive went on to say that he hopes GTA 6 feels "both familiar and entirely new," and above all else, something that people find to be fun.

"This is a narrative set in a world of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes," he added.

Finally, Houser reminded people that GTA 6 might be the pinnacle of the franchise so far, but Rockstar isn't closing up shop anytime soon.

"We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you," he said.

It's possible it won't be another 13 years for the next GTA game, as Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, has said the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will change.

Sam Houser rarely releases statements, gives interviews, or appears in Rockstar's promotional efforts, so even this celebratory statement is notable. GQ writer Sam White recently posted a series of tweets (and then deleted them) saying an interview he had planned with Sam Houser fell apart at the last minute.

On GTA 6, Sam Houser was involved in every aspect of the game's creative process.

Sam Houser's brother, Dan Houser, left Rockstar in 2020 after the successful launch of Red Dead Redemption II. He started a new company, Absurd Ventures, which is working on an open-world comedy game that will be revealed soon.

#3538. Wife, Daughter Arrested 4 Years After Man's Severed Head Was Found: Sheriff

A California man’s wife and daughter have been arrested in his murder more than four years after the discovery of his severed head inside a trash bag, authorities said.

The breakthrough comes after cold case investigators eventually identified the male victim as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr., who lived in Citrus Heights with his wife and daughter, according to the Placer County Sheriff’s Office.

Authorities were initially unable to identify him due to decomposition after his severed head was found in the Todd Valley area of Foresthill on September 28, 2024, authorities said.

An investigation revealed Fitzmaurice’s daughter, Mary Fitzmaurice, allegedly killed him inside their home and then worked with her mother, Fitzmaurice’s wife Georgia “Gwenn” Fitzmaurice, to get rid of his body, the Placer County Sheriff’s Office said in a Wednesday, November 18, news release.

Mary, 45, was taken into custody on murder charges while Georgia, 75, was arrested on accessory charges, according to the agency.

Paul had never been reported missing, authorities said. Mary and Georgia are accused of maintaining to friends and family that he was alive while they allegedly collected his Social Security checks and pension, per The Sacramento Bee.

Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire said at a Wednesday news conference that the office plans to file murder charges against Mary in connection with Paul’s death, according to the newspaper.

“And we will continue to evaluate the investigation to determine if additional charges related to the murder on behalf of Gwenn are appropriate, as well as additional charges related the collecting of those [Social Security and pension] benefits,” Gire said, referring to Georgia by her nickname.

It wasn’t immediately clear whether Mary and Georgia had retained legal counsel.

The rest of Paul’s remains haven’t been found to date, according to authorities.

Mary and Georgia were taken into custody on Tuesday, November 17, after detectives executed a search warrant at their Citrus Heights home, the district attorney’s office said.

A potential motive for Paul’s murder wasn’t specified by law enforcement.

“We are grateful to the FBI for its assistance throughout the investigation, including the work of its Evidence Response Team during the execution of a search warrant at the residence,” the sheriff’s office said in a statement. “We also appreciate the support of the Citrus Heights Police Department and the Contra Costa County Crime Lab, which provided advanced DNA testing of evidence.”

Over the years, Shonda Rhimes has been taking over television with dramas and romances that people can’t get enough of. Thanks to streaming, fans are able to rewatch and discover her projects. Scandal, for instance, is arguably one of Rhimes’ best shows, even eight years after its final season aired. Unfortunately, those streaming it with a Netflix subscription will soon have to say goodbye, meaning I have to say goodbye to one of my favorite TV couples, too.

For the second time since initially being added to Netflix back in 2014, Scandal is set to leave the streaming giant in December. This comes less than two years after the political drama rejoined Netflix in June 2025, five years after it originally left. Fans will have until December 17 to watch all seven seasons, and it’s unknown if Scandal will be added to Netflix again.

The reason for Scandal’s departure from Netflix likely has to do with the licensing agreement with the streamer expiring. However, it’s unknown if another deal will be made. It’s definitely disappointing, considering Scandal was one of the best shows on television, and soon, a lot of people won’t be able to watch it. All seven seasons are available to stream on the Disney-owned platform, and there’s no indication that it will be leaving. So fans will be able to catch all of Scandal’s biggest moments, and it means that I can still watch Olivia and Fitz.

I’m not one to wish for the downfall of a couple and root for an affair, but when it comes to Scandal, it’s kind of hard not to. Kerry Washington’s Olivia Pope and Tony Goldwyn’s President Fitzgerald “Fitz” Thomas Grant III were the couple on Scandal. They had a tumultuous relationship as they denied feelings for one another pretty early on, since Olivia had worked on Fitz’s campaign and was the White House Director of Communications. Not to mention the fact that Fitz was married to Melody “Mellie” Margaret Grant (Bellamy Young). He later divorced her, and she was thriving without him, so it definitely all worked out in the end.

However, with their secret sessions and sexual tension, as well as the fact that Fitz would have literally given the country to save Olivia when she was taken, their relationship was just too good to be an affair. No one was able to keep them apart. Of course, it wasn’t always easy, especially after their relationship and affair became public knowledge, but they always found their way back to each other.

Even today, Olitz remains a favorite with fans. The couple is still talked about online, with plenty of edits going around on TikTok. It helps that Washington and Goldwyn still have love for the series and their on-screen relationship as well. They’ve reunited on numerous occasions over the years, both for events and personally. Goldwyn has even shared his hope that Washington would appear on Law & Order, and she has shared that same sentiment. He admitted back in 2025 that he keeps “bugging her” about it, so maybe a reunion on another show could happen.

Plus, we'll always have Olivia and Fitz. Well, we won't always have them on Netflix, because Scandal is leaving on December 17. However, if you'd like to keep watching the show, you can stream it on Hulu too.

#3532. I Played Wendy's RPG, and It's Actually Worth It for the Free Food

November is a huge month for video games. Nintendo dropped its remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the Switch 2 last week, and the long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI is right around the corner. But the game we've been waiting for most of all also launched this month: WendyQuest, the free RPG from Wendy's. (No, this is not a joke.)

Despite the absurdity of a hamburger chain making a full video game (complete with Wendy's-themed puns), the thing is, this game is pretty solid—even if it is a promotion at the end of the day. WendyQuest's main purpose is to offer customers coupons they can use toward purchases in real life, though it's a bit of a commitment. It took me just under an hour of gameplay before I earned my first coupon, and Wendy's says it takes roughly 15 hours to beat. All that to say, this is a pretty unique marketing campaign.

I was surprised booting up WendyQuest on my iPhone. This doesn't necessarily feel like a thrown-together product. On the flip side, the production quality is quite high. The music is solid and very much traditionally RPG; there are even three save slots, in case you plan to return to this RPG again and again.

There's even a story, albeit cheesy (no pun intended): As the game explains, the "Four Great Spirits of Flavor" created Savoria, "a food-rich paradise." All was well until Mech Corp, led by the evil Dr. MechBorg, built robots to take over Savoria. The plot is far from compelling, and the writing can be a little over the top, but hey, I'll give them credit: They thought through a full story here.

You play as Wendy, the "representation of true culinary excellence and taste as dictated by the four ancient spirits of flavor." Wendy (or The Wendy, as some call her) is tasked with saving the world, traveling between villages and picking up new characters along the way. The game world even has "real" Wendy's locations you can visit. These act like inns and shops in other RPGs, giving you a chance to heal while also buying equipment.

Like other RPGs, WendyQuest uses turn-based combat. You have to charge up your attacks, but stop before they hit 100%, or you'll miss. (It took me a while to master the timing.) I'm pretty impressed with how challenging some of these battles can be, though you are quickly given the option of an amulet that gives you a huge leg-up in combat. You don't have to take it, but it makes fights easier if you're only in it for the coupons. That, combined with the spatulas the game encourages you to buy, lets you mow down enemies. You can also utilize your companions here: "Frygor," for example, can either attack enemies with a barrage of fries, or use those fries to build a shield to protect you.

While there are tons of enemies to fight, the key baddies are the "mechs." There are five in total, and after you defeat each, you get a coupon. Spoiler alert: The first mech drops the "Fry Stone," which nets you a coupon for a free order of medium fries—though you need to buy something in tandem, as well as use the Wendy's app. While I stopped my gaming here for this article, the other four coupons are:

Free biscuit or croissant (I didn't even know Wendy's sold biscuits and croissants)

Again, it's wild that WendyQuest has a 10+ hour campaign, with over 1,000 lines of dialogue to boot. I'm not sure this is a game I'm going to see through to the end, but I'll admit, it's a fun marketing approach from Wendy's. Sure, they could have run a promotion in the Wendy's app to give people coupons, but instead, they built an entire RPG. I respect it. You can download the game for iOS, Android, or Steam.

#3531. Don’t Expect To See Vice City For A Long Time In GTA 6

For those still waiting for GTA 6 to unlock, it's possible you have something of a mistaken impression of what the early hours will look like. Despite partially sharing a setting with GTA Vice City, you should not expect to be walking up the game's equivalent of Ocean Drive and Miami Beach in the opening minutes, as in the 2002 game. Far from it.

As we noted in our video discussion on why we gave GTA 6 a 10/10 in our review, Tamoor and Jake did some expectation-setting. Rather than starting the game in Vice City, you'll instead spend the opening hours in a smaller corner of the state of Leonida, Key Lento. Vice City is undoubtedly the crown jewel of the game's world, but it could be as much as 20 hours before you reach it, depending on how you play.

This seems to be a deliberate decision that, as Tam says, allows you to progress through the world at roughly the same pace as the ambitions of co-stars Lucia and Jason. The opening area may not be as glamorous as Vice City, but it is no less detailed than the rest of the game. It's possible it's only meant to last you around 5-6 hours, but we found it easy to get lost spending far more time than that, which resulted in Tam not reaching Vice City until after 15 or 16 hours.

Key Lento provides a good look at how the game and its simulation work, letting you eventually progress to a much larger space (seriously, the map is huge) with a good understanding of how things work.

All of this is to say, the glitz and glamor of Vice City are waiting for you--eventually. To make the most of the opening hours, be sure to check out our guide on what to do in GTA 6 first.

There are so many A+ celebrity bromances, from Matt Damon and Ben Affleck to Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman. The two Oscar winners have been friends for years, and a hallmark of the relationship is that the two enjoy taking playful shots at each other. That recently continued during some red carpet interviews, and I’m so glad this trolling between the two prank war participants is still going strong.

Brad Pitt recently stepped out for the Los Angeles premiere of his latest 2026 movie schedule entry, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, where he spoke with ET. During the chat, the news outlet referenced some recent comments that Pitt’s longtime friend and frequent co-star made about his dance moves. Never one to let a joke go unanswered, Pitt humorously clapped back with a take on Clooney’s opinion. Watch Clooney share his initial comments and Pitt drop his rebuttal in the Instagram video below:

A post shared by Entertainment Tonight (@entertainmenttonight)

Spoken like two men who have a friendly rivalry of sorts, and this dynamic goes back quite a while. It was especially present when the pair worked together on the Ocean’s Trilogy, which began back in 2001. Since then, the two have kept their relationship playful, which has led to some great moments. Even earlier this year, Pitt – while promoting his canine-centric movie, Heart of the Beast – mused that a dog could’ve replaced Clooney in Ocean’s Eleven. That’s a great jab but, still, I love Clooney’s take on being able to outdance Pitt:

Of course, the self-deprecating actor also clarified that he couldn’t say with certainty that he’d outdo Clooney. Ocean’s Fourteen is in the works, with the surviving cast members reportedly reprising their roles. I look forward to seeing him and Brad Pitt share the screen again, and I also hope that we can look forward to many more years of them trolling each other.

#3528. Bigfoot Is Back In GTA 6, And Apparently He Smells Revolting

Grand Theft Auto games have been home to some weird phenomena over the years, and in GTA 6, it looks like Bigfoot is back and stinkier than ever. As the game steadily rolls out worldwide--or as people digitally immigrate to New Zealand for early access--streamers have been posting clips online of their encounters with the cryptid, and this time, it doesn't look like a man in a suit.

It looks like the Bigfoot sighting is tied to a mission in GTA 6, as the mysterious creature is wandering the woods of Leonida and it takes off in a panic when you encounter it. Another clip shows a strange encounter in the woods, with the player interacting with an effigy that emits noxious fumes and knocks them out. In a brief cutscene, Bigfoots, uh, really big feet, can be seen approaching Jason as he drifts in and out of consciousness.

In that first clip, Bigfoot is also covered in a cloud of fumes, which likely references stories about the mythical creature's potent stench. For GTA--and Red Dead Redemption--fans, this isn't the first time that they've been involved in a Bigfoot sighting, as encounters with it stretch back decades.

Back in 2004, rumors began to circulate about Bigfoot existing in GTA: San Andreas, but Rockstar dismissed these reports as false in 2005. A few years later, in Red Dead Redemption's Undead Nightmare expansion, protagonist John Marston was tasked with hunting down a pack of Sasquatches, and it was eventually revealed that the creatures were peaceful, capable of human speech, and now going extinct thanks to a certain trigger-happy cowboy.

Bigfoot would appear in GTA 5, as getting 100% completion in the game would unlock a new mission where co-protagonist Franklin hunts down a creature in Blaine Woods, only to discover it was a man in a costume. As an extra joke, the Bigfoot impersonator drops a few references to Red Dead Redemption's infamous encounter, but that doesn't mean the real Bigfoot isn't lurking in GTA 5. You could use the thermal scope on the sniper rifle supplied to you to spot a bipedal creature watching you during the "Predator" mission, and eating a golden Peyote plant under specific environmental conditions would turn players into Bigfoot.

Red Dead Redemption 2 brought an air of mystery back to the Bigfoot mythos, as you could find a gigantic skeleton half-buried in the snow high up on Mount Shann, and protagonist Arthur Morgan could also speak to an unseen figure that was heavily implied to be Bigfoot.

Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The hype surrounding the long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI has reached a fevered pitch, with reviews for the game universally saying it’s living up to that hype. The GTA series has consistently been one of the most popular gaming franchises of all time, and one of the most successful entertainment franchises on Earth. It’s also one of the only monster franchises that hasn’t been adapted as a movie or a TV show.

That’s always surprised me, because it seems ripe for a video game adaptation, right? Now, the CEO of Take-Two Interactive, the company that owns Rockstar, the studio that produces the games, was recently asked about a possible adaptation. His answer is actually kind of positive news, though hardly concrete evidence that an adaptation is on the way.

While appearing on The David Rubenstein Show, CEO Strauss Zelnick was asked about the possibility of a movie. He responded:

We're very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company, and our goal is to make the best entertainment on Earth.  Entertainment we’re always proud of. We would make a movie or a television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it, if they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. It's a high bar to do that, and, of course, there's always a risk of failure. So we don't rule it out, but we're very, very selective.

“Line extensions” are when business use existing products or intellectual property to expand how they can take advantage of markets, like, for example, video game movie adaptations. Take-Two, as Zelnick points out, has been very careful with how they’ve expanded their brands outside of video games. No franchise shows that more than GTA. It seems ripe for adaptation and really has been for decades, but they have yet to pull the trigger. They do seem open to it, though.

Like millions of other people, I’m still waiting for a few more hours to be able to play GTA VI, as we all have been for years now. Based on the glowing reviews, this could be the version of the game most likely to get adapted into a movie. Reviews have talked about the storyline in the new game, praising it for how well the story is incorporated into the game. It seems full of drama (and great music). Plus, there are two playable protagonists, a couple named Jason and Lucia.

This is the first time GTA has featured a female playable character, and it tells the story of the two, which to me sounds like the perfect basis for a possible film. While the characters in previous versions have been fun, these two actually sound like the most realistic characters, with a deep backstory together. That really leaves the option open.

It’s also worth mentioning that Zelnick, who took over Take-Two in 2007, has a history in the movie world as the former President of 20th Century Fox and overseeing hit movies like Home Alone and before that worked for Columbia Pictures Television. If anyone knows how to strike a good deal for Take-Two, it’s Zelnick. I would love to see it happen one day!

#3522. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two’s Stock Adds Billions After Rave Reviews, But It’s Not All Good News

After more than 10 years of waiting, Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally available now (at least in New Zealand and Australia). The anticipation has been sky-high for both consumers and investors alike, and Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, is seeing a huge uplift in its share price today after the game's overwhelmingly positive reviews landed.

Take-Two shares rose by nearly7% in pre-market trading today, and moved higher from there as the day went on. This meant that Take-Two's market cap grew by billions today alone.

Stock analysts expected share value to increase in the lead-up to launch, and many expect it to go higher still due to the expected launches of GTA Online and a PC edition of the game in 2027.

While Take-Two's stock price is popping today, Take-Two remains down close to 20% so far in 2026 and is down about 15% over the past 12 months. Why? No one really knows, because the stock market is fickle. Take-Two's stock price got hammered earlier this year when Google announced new AI software to make games, presumably spooking investors. The stock has not recovered since.

The 52-week high for Take-Two is $265.65, and the 52-week low is $183.86.

Zooming further out, though, Take-Two has been a fantastic investment for people who bought and held for a long time. As Rand Group points out, $10,000 invested into Take-Two when GTA 5 launched in 2013 has grown to more than $120,000 today.

GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the game a rare 10/10. "GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," reviewer Tamoor Hussain said.

GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever.

Obsession is that one film on the 2026 movie schedule that we can’t stop talking about, and why would we want to? Now we can stream it to our heart's content with a Netflix subscription, I needed to dig up all the fun behind-the-scenes facts I learned from writer/director Curry Barker. Each of these made me think of the movie in a whole different way! Let’s get into it. (SPOILERS ahead.)

I’m always curious about how movies change over time, and Barker told CinemaBlend about one pivotal scene that he played around with a lot. The writer/director was also the movie’s editor on the $750k independent production, and he told us about one exchange he tried a bunch of different ways . In his words:

The scene where they’re driving and she’s talking about romance and love. And she’s saying, like, ‘Hey, you know, you’re the only person I can talk to about this stuff.’ That scene changed so much. There’s probably like ten different versions of that scene. One that’s a little longer, one that’s shorter, one where she doesn’t even say the line, one where she goes into a longer thing. Like, I don’t know why. That scene just has so many different versions of it.

This sort of blew my mind because this is the scene I was playing over and over in my head after seeing the movie. It’s an important scene because it establishes Bear and Nikki’s relationship before Nikki loses her autonomy. Watching that scene made me wonder if Bear could have had a shot with Nikki if he had simply asked her out rather than using the One Wish Willow. With that in mind, I totally see why this scene would have needed tweaking, but I think it's perfect now.

When I first watched Obsession, I felt a chill down my spine when Bear called the number on the back of the One Wish Willow box. Then, I subsequently had so many questions about what was going on! When I talked to Barker about this scene, he revealed he was the one on the other side of the line.

Well, that was me… yeah, that’s my voice. He works for the One Wish Willow Company, he kind of answers their phone calls. He handles all the complaints of all the wishes. But, there’s no, I mean, I like to keep it pretty vague. I think you could think of it as some sort of purgatory that [Nikki’s] being kept in, right?

What a fun cameo! I had no idea Barker was the voice, but it’s a fun little tidbit I’ll always think about when I watch that scene. He gave us some interesting insight about what’s going on with that phone call, too. I'm never forgetting Nikki's screams on the other line.

One more BTS detail I want to share has to do with what didn’t make it into the film. Obsession really goes hard in the paint on the movie rating scale, so I was curious if there was a scene the director had to remove because it went too far. The answer is, yes, there was one moment.

There was only one thing I had to take out because it was too far, but other than that they really let me do whatever they wanted. And, I was kind of, like, shocked. This movie really felt like a bunch of kids getting together and making something, and hoping that the parents don’t come home. They never did. Nobody ever stopped us, and we just kept making the thing we wanted to make. Like, even the way we shot it. We thought someone was going to tell us to turn the lights on.

So, what was that “one thing”? During a Q&A (via Deadline), Barker revealed it was the scene where Nikki kills Sarah by smashing her head into the steering wheel. Barker said there was originally “about six or seven more smashes." The MPA ratings board was going to give the movie a NC-17 rating because of it. At first, Barker wasn’t happy about making the change, but when he saw the movie with an audience (and heard their reactions), he realized the number they landed on was “the right number” to choose.

You can check out the rest of our Obsession interview on CinemaBlend's YouTube. There we also talked about that gross cat scene and what probably happens after the ending. I know I’m always finding new theories online. Obsession really is the movie of the year for this horror fan, and I loved learning these behind-the-scenes facts.

#3520. Update Your iPhone to Prevent People From Seeing iMessages They Shouldn't

Has this ever happened to you? You add someone new to an iMessage group chat, and wonder, "Huh, can they see any of the messages from before they were added?" The answer to that question is supposed to be "no." By design, new iMessage group chat members are only privy to texts that arrive after they were added. When they join, it's essentially a blank slate, as if you just created the group for the first time. At least, that's how it's intended to work.

As it turns out, there's a bug with iMessage that may allow new group chat members to see texts from before they were added to the chat. That's a problem, and not just for the iPhone users out there talking smack about people before inviting them to join the group chat. It means iMessage, and Apple's platforms in general, aren't working like they're supposed to be. You don't have to be talking behind people's backs to not want new members seeing existing chats. Maybe you're planning a surprise party for someone, and add them to the group once everyone's in on the plan; maybe the texts in the chat aren't relevant to the current group, and the person joining simply does not need to access them.

That's not all: There exists another security flaw that could allow remote hackers to join an iMessage group and receive new messages. You might add a new user to a group chat and inadvertently invite them to read all existing messages, while at the same time being attacked by a bad actor who can then intercept all future messages. Not good.

Luckily, there's currently a fix for these problems. Apple patched (and revealed) the bugs, along with seven other security flaws, with a series of software updates on Monday for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro. Not all of the updates include patches for these two iMessage flaws—specifically, some of the updates for older Apple devices. But the rest, including iOS 27.2.1, macOS 27.2.1, macOS 26.7.3, macOS 15.8.3, watchOS 27.2.1, and visionOS 27.2.1, include the iMessage patches.

Each update includes its own list of patches, but, for this article, I'll take a look at the nine patches in iOS 27.2.1. You'll find the two iMessage bugs, plus seven other patches, in the list below:

AirPlay: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113968: Apple

App Intents: Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113963: László Várady

Bluetooth: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed with improved memory management. CVE-2026-113970: Apple

brotli: Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption. Description: An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation. CVE-2026-111497

CoreUtils: Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction. Description: This issue was addressed with improved checks. CVE-2026-113965: Apple

CoreUtils: Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages. Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation. CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher

Messages: Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined. Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher

Rapportd: Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts. Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management. CVE-2026-113969: Apple

For a full accounting of the patches included in the other security updates, check out Apple's official security releases site.

To install Apple's latest security updates, you'll simply need to update your device as you usually do. On iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro, head to Settings > General > Software Update; on Mac, go to System Settings > General > Software Update. Here, follow the on-screen instructions to download and install the latest version of your device's software.

#3519. How Xbox’s Streaming Deal For GTA 6 Could Expand Its Marketshare By 30%

Microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92.

This is according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which said the streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%.

For anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA 6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, or even an Xbox One.

There are some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that might not be an issue for everyone.

No such arrangement is in place for PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox. Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the PS5.

Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units, but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all.

Beyond this, Ampere said there could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6 streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger position to serve a large influx of users streaming a brand-new game like GTA 6 compared to Sony." 

"The favorable distribution costs to Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 users can generally stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience."

Beyond all this, Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580) over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more important to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said.

Under $100 to play GTA 6 on Xbox

Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6, a controller, and a screen.

Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be 0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming, assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game.

This rate leaves little margin for Xbox, Ampere said, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in accounts that is never used."

As announced previously, people can stream GTA 6 to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a Game Pass membership. The pricing is below.

Cloud playtime packs pricing:

  • 10 hours for $4
  • 25 hours for $8
  • 50 hours for $12

Coinciding with GTA 6's release and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are:

  • Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours
  • Game Pass Premium: 10 hours
  • Game Pass Essential: 5 hours

Even beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6 considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for the cheapest new PS5.

GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

#3517. Taylor Swift Wears 'Toy Story' Yellow at 2026 CMA Awards After 10-Years Away

Taylor Swift lassoed up a chic red carpet outing — and brought the sunshine with her bold Toy Story-approved gown — at the 2026 CMA Awards.

All eyes were on Swift, 36, as she hit the scene on Wednesday, November 18, solo at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena, where she was dressed to the nines in a bright yellow strapless gown from the Oscar de la Renta Spring/Summer 2027 Ready to Wear collection.

For glam, the pop star wore her blonde locks twisted up in a chic updo with her wispy bangs framing her face. She rocked sexy, gold high heels that gave a bit of a snake-style vibe and finished her look with an orange-red lip. As one red carpet host said, the singer was “dripping”in diamonds, head-to-toe.

Swift, who last attended the CMAs in 2016 and is set to perform on Wednesday, is nominated for “Single of the Year” alongside Ella Langley, Lainey Wilson and Cody Johnson.

“Looks like I haven’t yee’d my last haw,” Swift wrote via her Instagram Stories at the time, celebrating her nomination. “See you there Nov 18.”

Swift previously won 12 CMAs trophies, hoping to add another for her song “I Knew It, I Knew You.” The singer wrote the track with longtime collaborator Jack Antonoff for the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, inspired by the backstory of cowgirl figurine Jessie (voiced by Joan Cusack).

“For Jessie, I feel like the line, ‘I watched you drive around the bend for what I thought would be the last time I saw my friend,’ that hits me really hard because that movie just broke my heart,” Swift recalled during the film’s 20/20 special in June. “So I’m really happy to, like, give her a happy moment. ”

According to Swift, she was particularly “grateful” to follow in composer Randy Newman’s footsteps. (Newman, 82, created the music for the entire Toy Story franchise. Swift is the only other musician who lent her vocal styling to the animated franchise’s soundtrack.)

“I felt wonderful knowing that I had Randy’s blessing to write for this film, given that I’m the first songwriter to get to partake in the Toy Story world outside of Randy,” Swift added at the time. “I was absolutely dazzled by [the movie]. It is my favorite Toy Story movie.”

“I Knew It, I Knew You” marked Swift’s return to the country music genre.

“I love my country roots more and more as I go further in this path,” she told attendees during a Grammy Museum event in August. “I wanna honor them more and more, the artist who shaped who I am, and that all happened in Nashville.”

Swift famously began her career as a country artist, eventually shifting toward pop music with 2014’s 1989. To date, Swift has released 12 studio albums and rerecorded four of her early albums.

#3516. This AirPods Feature Fixed My Biggest Problem With Listening to Podcasts to Fall Asleep

We're highlighting the small changes—from useful new gadgets, to fresh productivity techniques, to efficient hacks—that are improving our lives on a weekly basis.

There's lots to recommend about podcasts (and lots of podcasts to recommend), but one of their biggest benefits—for me, anyway—has little to do with what a particular show is about or even who hosts it: They're great for dissociating. I often have a podcast playing to distract my anxious brain from whatever I'm worried about (which, in 2026, is usually slightly less than everything).

Any time I don't want to be alone with my thoughts (say, when commuting or doing mindless chores), I can put on a podcast and be entertained by a couple of goobers talking about movies rather than spinning my wheels about my son's middle school applications. And there's no time I want to distance myself from reality more than bedtime.

For years I've used podcasts as a non-pharmaceutical sleep aid, and few things are more effective at helping me drop off quickly. Unfortunately, for years this also meant that once I fell asleep, the podcast kept playing. I have my podcast app set to delete episodes once finished, so if it was a show I cared about, I'd need to do a lot of redownloading and scrubbing through to find where I left off—that is, until I upgraded my earbuds to the AirPods Pro 3.

The AirPods Pro 3 launched alongside iOS 26 in the fall of 2025 with flashy features like vastly improved noise cancellation, Live Translation, Heart Rate Sensing, and hearing health settings, all of them quite welcome on a set of $250 premium earbuds. But the best new AirPods feature was one I didn't even know about when I decided to upgrade my four-year-old Beats Fit Pro.

In the AirPods settings (accessible via your iPhone's Settings app), if you tap Audio & Routing and scroll down, you'll see an option to turn on a setting called Pause Media When Falling Asleep. I don't think I need to tell you what this setting does. I can tell you that it works great.

According to Apple, the feature works by sensing when you're drifting off using the earbuds' built-in accelerometer to track your movement (or lack thereof). Once your earbuds have determined that you're falling asleep, they will pause your audio for you. And it isn't just the 2025 AirPods Pro 3 that support it—it also works on the second-generation AirPods Pro as well as the AirPods 4 and the AirPods 5.

I'll admit that I don't really understand how the AirPods Pro 3 can tell I'm falling asleep versus just lying very still, but I've never had them pause accidentally during active listening. Conversely, whenever I go back to the podcast I was listening to the night before, I'll find that the audio paused within a minute or two of the last part I remember hearing.

The AirPods Pro 3 aren't the only earbuds with a feature like this, but you'll most often only find it in dedicated "sleep earbuds" designed specifically for the purpose. While many of those offer extra health features like the ability to track your sleep cycles, I'm not really interested in that (my Apple Watch does most of it, and I don't look at that data anyway). Pausing my audio when I'm asleep is really all I need, and the AirPods Pro 3 do it well enough that I don't need to bother with a pair of dedicated bedtime buds.

The goal of sharing a Saturday Night Live sketch is typically to elicit a laugh, but now and again, one makes such a thoughtful or important point that people use it as a conversation starter or as evidence to prove a point. That’s exactly what’s going on with last weekend’s Sister sketch, a fake commercial about how caregiving responsibilities overwhelmingly fall on the women in the family. Tens of thousands have taken to social media to share or retweet the sketch alongside comments about how they feel seen, and now, we’ve reached the point where people are using it to call out their own family members.

Sister has been watched more than five million times in the past few days on YouTube, more than twenty million times on X and untold millions of times more on additional social platforms. If you look at comments on any of these platforms, two immediate themes jump out. Many people are saying they feel exactly like the title sister in the sketch, and many others are calling out family members for not helping with caregiving responsibilities.

Actually, I probably phrased that second one too nicely. What many people are doing is throwing up their middle fingers at family members and telling stories about their avoidance and/ or woeful incompetence. Here’s a story with more than 69,000 likes…

My mom literally called me to come over to help her water a single outdoor plant, and when I got there she was cooking for my older brother who had been there the entire time.

That wild story is definitely not an outlier either. The angry rants are just pouring out of people, an overwhelming majority of whom are women who feel like they are left doing everything while their siblings live their lives. Some are mad about how they did everything until their parent died, only to find out their absentee sibling(s) got the exact same inheritance. Others are mad about how their family members infrequently show up and then critique the job they were doing and question the decisions they make.

One woman shared that a caretaker in her family was later sued by the surviving family members for taking money out of the disabled parent’s bank account to buy said parent food and medicine. You can check out that banger below, which has about five thousand likes…

With Sister you can also wait for her to spend your dad’s money on essentials for him like groceries or clothes and then sue her later - because she never had financial power of attorney!

Seriously, don’t take my word for it. Look wherever the Sister sketch is embedded. You’ll immediately start running into story after story of angry people who need to let it out. I saw one woman calling out the parent they’re looking after for raising her brother to think he didn’t need to help. I’ve seen numerous lawyers, nurses, dementia care workers and doctors saying they see the same dynamic over and over again. I saw one woman say her brother who lives near her mom can’t be bothered to help; so, she has to travel across the country to handle things.

watching this from my mom’s house 1500 miles away bc my brother Just Can’t Manage to get her to the doctor or the dentist. he lives down the street

It’s clear this sketch, which is filled with fun little easter eggs, struck a nerve, but it seems like in a very therapeutic way. It’s allowing people to give voice to frustrations they’ve clearly had for a long time, and if it leads to even some family members doing a little self-reflecting and helping out a bit more, it’ll be a huge victory. You can watch the sketch in full below...

Saturday Night Live is off for a few weeks for the holidays, but it’ll return in early December with the next new episode guest hosted by Amanda Seyfried. Fingers crossed she’s able to give us something that makes even a fraction of the cultural footprint. You can catch previously aired episodes streaming with a Peacock subscription.

#3513. Who Killed Fashion Founders Bryan Walker and Michelle Min?

Panoramic Hill looms above the UC Berkeley campus, a tree-covered neighborhood cut by steep paths and outdoor staircases. Century-old homes by brand-name architects like Bernard Maybeck and Walter Steilberg dot the incline, which straddles the border of Berkeley and Oakland. Each residence is worth millions; increase the amount for the occasional bit of newer construction. Unlike the busy urban streets below, the area is incredibly quiet. That’s one of the reasons everyone heard the shots.

“I have that stored in my memory, as I will for the rest of my life,” Daniella Salzman tells me, looking out her window at the former home of Michelle Min and her husband, Bryan Walker. The couple, creators of the Bryn Walker clothing brand, were found just outside their residence around 10:45 a.m. on October 2, 2026, shortly after neighbors called 911 to report the sound of gunfire. Initial confusion about jurisdiction sent police from both Berkeley’s and Oakland’s departments to the scene.

By the time paramedics arrived, Walker and Min were dead from what OPD assistant chief Casey Johnson characterized as “apparent gunshots” in a press conference later that day. A firearm, he said, was located at the scene. He declined to offer further details on the case, saying that the department’s homicide division would handle the investigation.

Nearly seven weeks later, we still know next to nothing about how Walker and Min died. While OPD turned down my request to speak with Johnson, it sent me a press release with the same details he laid out on October 2. Follow-up questions were met with: “There are no updates being released other than the information below.”

Bryn Walker store on Vine Street in Berkeley, California.

“I don’t know what has publicly been shared or what privately has been learned about what took place,” Salzman says carefully. Police have been silent since the brief press conference the day the bodies were discovered. But Michelle Min’s brother, Paul Min, hasn’t been quiet.

Within two days after his 63-year-old sister was found dead, Paul spoke with outlets including the LA Times and the California Post, accusing his brother-in-law of killing his wife, then himself, following a series of disastrous financial decisions that led to significant losses and a collapse in his mental state. The interviews, given so soon after the crime, suggest Paul was still in a state of shock over his loss. Walker, who was 61 when he died, was “the most honest, responsible, hardworking guy you have ever known,” Paul told the LA Times. “I loved him like a brother.” Michelle “was utterly devoted to Bryan to the very end,” Paul told the Post, “and he shot her.”

After those interviews, which were published that first weekend in October, Paul fell silent too; I made multiple efforts to arrange an interview but was ultimately unsuccessful. But according to the Post’s interview, Walker “had quietly taken out loans against their properties, and had gambled on risky options and leveraged positions,” with estimated losses of “well over $100 million.” The debt, per the LA Times story, allegedly prompted Walker to suggest that he and the Min siblings “end things”—a proposal that alarmed the Mins, but only because of its implications for Walker’s mental health. Paul didn’t see Walker as a danger: “He said the idea that Walker would or could harm them was absurd to the two of them,” reported the Times.

The Mins came to the US from Korea in 1977, settling first near Kansas City. Michelle met Walker there in the 1980s, and after the Mins’ parents chose to move to California, the siblings, and Walker, followed. In 1992 the couple opened a clothing store in Berkeley that sold goods from other makers. As time went on, they began to manufacture more and more of their own goods.

Eventually, Bryn Walker evolved into a clothing brand known for loose linen looks with an Asian-meets-Swedish flair. “Flowy, a touch eclectic, made for perhaps older women who want to mesh elegant/sophisticated with a bit of boho uniqueness,” a longtime Berkeley resident told me over email. “Women who want to look expensive but with a bit of verve.” When I described the company to one San Francisco resident as “elevated Chico’s,” I got a stern look. “You better not let any of the Bryn Walker moms at Lowell hear you say that,” she said, referencing the city’s hotly competitive public high school. “These are not humorous people.”

Bryn Walker store on Fourth Street in Berkeley, California.

According to the Post piece, Walker “had stepped aside and allowed his designer wife to control their mutual business and his eponymous fashion label,” but it’s not clear when that management change occurred. As the brand grew, it struck a chord with fashion businesses across the country—from luxury boutiques to the family-run department store chain Dillard’s. Bryn Walker also opened its own brick-and-mortar storefronts beyond Berkeley.

Many of those stores are now gone. One Bryn Walker location in Santa Monica closed prior to mid-March of 2021, while a 22-year-old outpost in Palo Alto shuttered in 2020. On the East Coast, a shop in Edgartown, on Martha’s Vineyard, went dark in 2024. A call to its shop in Vineyard Haven was met with a recorded message saying the business would be closed until further notice. That leaves just two company-owned shops, both in Berkeley, where Bryn Walker began.

One of those stores is on Berkeley’s buzzy Fourth Street, a glossy shopping destination lined with outposts of national brands like Apple, Lululemon, and Herman Miller. With items generally priced between $130–$300, it fits right into the overall ethos of that street—and Berkeley—where almost everything is spendy but not flashy; theoretically accessible, though not to those on a budget. During my recent visit to the shop, the sole staffer remained pleasant even after I identified myself as a journalist—but her tone grew firm. “It’s all still too raw,” she said of the tragedy.

I asked if, as he’d said he would in his Post interview, Paul Min had taken over management of the company following its founders’ deaths. “I don’t know about that,” she replied, before declining to speak further. I was told by another local business owner that Bryn Walker employees are actively seeking other employment; it’s unclear what will happen to the label now that its creators are gone. I tried to reach Bryn Walker management by phone and email for this story, but did not receive a response.

Emilie Raguso was one of the first journalists to report on the deaths, for her independent outlet, The Berkeley Scanner. As she began investigating, she “saw that the number of open shops was different based on where you looked,” she says. “I was getting this early inkling of what others later reported as far as the business being in trouble.”

“The writing was on the wall,” she continues, “but there was nothing explicit. It did seem like, Oh, this is not a thriving business.”

Paul’s comments to the media didn’t address the health of the business. Instead, he was focused on Walker and Michelle’s personal finances, which he alleged were laid to waste by Walker’s mismanagement. “Your spouse lied to you and lost over $100 million and you might be out on the streets,” Paul told the Post. “You might go from being one of the wealthiest people in the country to being homeless because your husband lied to you and wagered everything on crazy bets.”

According to Paul, things grew so grim for Walker that the Mins spoke about institutionalizing him. But it’s also unclear how they would have acted on that without Walker’s cooperation. California enacted its CARE Court program in 2023, more easily allowing court-ordered treatment plans for those who might pose a threat to themselves or others. But in practice, courts have been reluctant to take that drastic step, frequently rejecting petitions from those closest to the person in crisis.

Bryn Walker-Pacific Cotton store on Main Street in Vineyard Haven, Massachusetts.

Speaking with the LA Times, Paul said that in Walker and Michelle’s home, he “found a note that lists a couple of [mental health] facilities. I speculate he saw that note or somehow figured out she was going to institutionalize him, but I have no idea.”

Paul’s claim that Walker killed Michelle over snowballing financial fears isn’t out of the realm of possibility, even in a place as wealthy as the Bay Area. One year before Walker and Michelle died, almost to the day, entrepreneur Paula Truong fatally shot her husband, Thomas, and their daughters, Mackenzie and Alexandra, before hanging herself in the garage of their $2.2 million San Francisco home. Reporting found that the family had experienced a string of financial challenges, including several failed business ventures, a home foreclosure, and a number of unpaid debts.

But that was in San Francisco—a sometimes gritty city that people escape with moves to places like Panoramic Hill. “When you get up into the hills, it does feel like a world apart,” Raguso says. “It feels insulated from a lot of the more common disturbances and things that we deal with down on the flatlands.”

Salzman has lived on that hill for more than 20 years, and she’s still struggling with the notion that her neighbor might have killed his wife. “Bryan was very engaged with neighbors who were needing support that were near him,” she says, characterizing him and Michelle as “committed to the community.” But she also believes that the fear of losing wealth can drive people to desperate acts. “We see wealth as being both our greatest need and our greatest opportunity here,” she says, “and we are told that we will be happy when we consume. This is the message that we’re given everywhere we look”—especially in a region with more billionaires than anywhere else in the world.

Raguso isn’t sure why Oakland police are taking so long to announce the results of their investigation. “At some point, there would be a ruling,” she says, citing possible delays with the medical examiner’s office as a reason things haven’t been resolved. According to Salzman, the vacuum of information has inspired her to look at all her neighbors with a little more care. “Part of what I awoke to was how little I know about really what’s going on with people that I’m geographically so close to,” she says.

“I just would have loved for there to have been a way to be a part of showing up for them, even around the little things. The more people that are aware of what is happening, the more people are potentially able to heal.”
